nodes.label: Getting Started with AI Training: A Beginner's Guide
RAFT (Retrieval Augmented Fine-Tuning) Methodology
nodes.rationale: RAFT trains models to distinguish oracle (relevant) context from distractor (irrelevant) context retrieved by BaseProcessor._build_augmented_requirements, so the AI learns which heading/info/interface items matter for a given requirement rather than treating all retrieved context as equally important.

nodes.label: Vision RAFT Training
nodes.rationale: Extends RAFT methodology to hybrid vision/text models (llama3.2-vision:11b) so the system learns to prioritize relevant diagrams and ignore distractor images, aiming for 40-60% better test case quality for visual requirements without full fine-tuning.

nodes.label: Hybrid Vision/Text Model Selection Strategy
nodes.rationale: Auto-select the vision model only when a requirement has a successfully saved image, falling back to the text model otherwise, to avoid unnecessary VRAM usage and cost when no visual context exists.

nodes.label: Canonical Test-Case Schema Normalization
nodes.rationale: The pipeline should define one canonical test-case schema (preconditions/test_steps, the fields the active adaptive_default template actually produces) and normalize AI output to it in one place after JSON parsing, because divergent field expectations across the deduplicator, validator, parser, and formatter caused silent false-positive deletion of legitimate test cases and always-false validation checks.

nodes.label: Vision Image Preprocessing for Memory Management
nodes.rationale: Resize/downsample and compress images (max 1024px, JPEG quality 85) during extraction before base64 encoding, to cap memory spikes from concurrent vision requests (achieved ~75% reduction, from ~216MB worst case to ~54MB) and avoid OOM crashes.
